propositions: A test subprocess-execs a shell script containing `rm -rf` against an interpolated variable without guards, risking unintended filesystem destruction when the variable is empty or unset
The static gate check_destructive_test_exec.py must flag unguarded destructive deletion patterns in subprocess-exec'd scripts and report path:line output matching existing lint gates
Remediated patterns using injectable seams (e.g. `${RM_CMD:-rm}`) or explicit guards (e.g. `: "${dir:?}"`) must pass the gate to avoid false positives on hardened call sites
The gate must run as part of `make lint` (enforced by pre-commit hook and CI) and exit non-zero on findings, not as a CI-provider-specific step
The gate's static analysis cannot prevent runtime mutations; dynamic OS sandbox controls provide load-bearing protection while this catches the pattern before merge
